question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away the Kaula teaching to the unworthy?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents immense wealth.
Such wealth may be accumulated by someone.
The verse sets up a comparison against giving the teaching.
inference: Even possession of wealth as vast as a jewel-filled ocean is not sufficient reason to transmit the teaching improperly.
uncertainties: The form ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is obscure and interpreted from context and transmission.
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels...
